# Training Method

First we must initialise the data from the previous file ` 02---Feature-Engineering-and-Selection` to create our analysis, so this is purely repeated:

```{r}
combined_data = read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Mathildelaunay/Sprint-1/refs/heads/main/Max%20Gold/combined_data.csv")

combined_data <- combined_data |>
  mutate(
    Date = dmy(Date),
    DayOfWeek = weekdays(Date),
    SeasonStart = if_else(
      month(Date) >= 8,
      year(Date),
      year(Date) - 1
    ),

    Season = paste0(
      SeasonStart,
      "/",
      substr(SeasonStart + 1, 3, 4)
    )
  )

features_1 = read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Mathildelaunay/Sprint-1/refs/heads/main/Max%20Gold/features_1.csv")
features_2 = read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Mathildelaunay/Sprint-1/refs/heads/main/Max%20Gold/features_2.csv")
features_5 = read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Mathildelaunay/Sprint-1/refs/heads/main/Max%20Gold/features_5.csv")
features_10 = read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Mathildelaunay/Sprint-1/refs/heads/main/Max%20Gold/features_10.csv")

```


```{r}
training_data <- combined_data |>
  filter(SeasonStart >= 2014,
         SeasonStart <= 2024,
         !is.na(HomeGoals),
         !is.na(AwayGoals)) |>
  mutate(
    DayOfWeek = factor(DayOfWeek))

testing_data <- combined_data |>
  filter(SeasonStart == 2025)

prediction_data <- combined_data |>
  filter(SeasonStart == 2026)

training_features_5 <- features_5 |>
  filter(
    SeasonStart >= 2014,
    SeasonStart <= 2024,
    !is.na(HomeGoals),
    !is.na(AwayGoals)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    DayOfWeek = factor(DayOfWeek)
    
  )

```

```{r}

home_data <- training_features_5 |>
  select(
    -Date,
    -SeasonStart,
    -HomeTeam,
    -AwayTeam,
    -AwayGoals,
    -Home_Wins,
    -Away_Wins
  )

away_data <- training_features_5 |>
  select(
    -Date,
    -SeasonStart,
    -HomeTeam,
    -AwayTeam,
    -HomeGoals, 
    -Home_Wins,
    -Away_Wins
  )

rf_home_initial <- randomForest(
  HomeGoals ~ .,
  data = home_data,
  ntree = 1000,
  importance = TRUE
)

importance_scores <- importance(rf_home_initial, type = 1)
importance_sorted <- sort(importance_scores[, 1], decreasing = TRUE)
home_features <- names(importance_sorted)[1:10]



rf_away_initial <- randomForest(
  AwayGoals ~ .,
  data = away_data,
  ntree = 1000,
  importance = TRUE
)


importance_scores_a <- importance(rf_away_initial, type = 1)
importance_sorted_a <- sort(importance_scores_a[, 1], decreasing = TRUE)
away_features <- names(importance_sorted_a)[1:10]
```

We will use $k=5$ and `ntree=1000` as a baseline to calculate our home and away features to be used in the sensitivity analysis, this keeps the sensitivity experiment controlled compared to the other $k$ values to create a correlation matrix between $k$ values. 

## Sensitivity Analysis 

We perform sensitivity analysis of $k$ and `ntree` in our random forest, where we take $k \in (1, 2, 5, 10)$ and `ntree = [250, 500, 1000, 1500]`. We apply our home and away random forests with varying parameters to create our training 




```{r}

training_features <- features_5 |>
  filter(
    SeasonStart >= 2014,
    SeasonStart <= 2024,
    !is.na(HomeGoals),
    !is.na(AwayGoals)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    DayOfWeek = factor(DayOfWeek)
    
  )


home_data <- training_features |>
  select(
    -Date,
    -SeasonStart,
    -HomeTeam,
    -AwayTeam,
    -AwayGoals,
    -Home_Wins,
    -Away_Wins
  )

away_data <- training_features |>
  select(
    -Date,
    -SeasonStart,
    -HomeTeam,
    -AwayTeam,
    -HomeGoals, 
    -Home_Wins,
    -Away_Wins
  )

rf_home_initial <- randomForest(
  HomeGoals ~ .,
  data = home_data,
  ntree = 1000,
  importance = TRUE
)

importance_scores <- importance(rf_home_initial, type = 1)
importance_sorted <- sort(importance_scores[, 1], decreasing = TRUE)
home_features <- names(importance_sorted)[1:10]



rf_away_initial <- randomForest(
  AwayGoals ~ .,
  data = away_data,
  ntree = 1000,
  importance = TRUE
)


importance_scores_a <- importance(rf_away_initial, type = 1)
importance_sorted_a <- sort(importance_scores_a[, 1], decreasing = TRUE)
away_features <- names(importance_sorted_a)[1:10]
X_home <- training_features |>
  select(all_of(home_features))

X_away <- training_features |>
  select(all_of(away_features))

set.seed(123)

rf_home <- randomForest(
  x = X_home,
  y = training_features$HomeGoals,
  ntree = 1000,
  mtry = floor(sqrt(ncol(X_home))),
  importance = TRUE
)

rf_away <- randomForest(
  x = X_away,
  y = training_features$AwayGoals,
  ntree = 1000,
  mtry = floor(sqrt(ncol(X_away))),
  importance = TRUE
)

```
